svg.title: Writing ઢ
svg.desc: 1 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ઢ (gujarati), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ઢ animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>. Source note on variation: The teaching app animates ઢ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper left, sweeps right across the high shoulder, descends through the middle into the left side of the broad outer lower bowl, circles around its base and right side, then continues directly around the small inner loop without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the high shoulder, broad outer bowl, and inner loop, but its printed shoulder is tighter and its bowl and counter more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's shoulder-to-outer-bowl-to-inner-loop order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the continuous run to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the shoulder, bowl, counter, loop, and terminal differently.
svg.text: How it is written — one unbroken stroke · 1 movement
